turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I’ve had severe vulvar itching that’s been slowly getting worse over the past year, and it hasn’t improved with over-the-counter lubricants. I also have significant pain during intercourse, so I’ve stopped having sex because of it.
How old are you, and have you gone through menopause?
I’m 60 years old, and I went through menopause at 52.
Have you noticed any visible changes to the skin in that area, such as whitening, thinning, thickening, cracks, or changes in the shape of your labia or vaginal opening?

I haven’t noticed any major changes in the shape of my labia or vaginal opening, but the area feels very irritated and sore, with a strong itch that’s gradually worse. I’m not sure whether there’s whitening, thinning, or thickening, because it’s mostly discomfort rather than something I can clearly see.
Have you experienced any bleeding, skin cracking (fissures), or open sores in that area, especially after scratching or during intercourse?

I haven’t had any bleeding, but the skin sometimes feels raw and tender, especially after scratching or after intercourse. I’m not seeing obvious open sores, fissures, or anything that looks like an ulcer.
Does the itching or irritation extend to the area around your anus, or is it strictly confined to the vulva?
“It mainly feels confined to the vulvar area, but sometimes I notice the irritation creeping toward the area around my anus—still it’s not as intense there as it is on the vulva.”
Have you tried any prescription treatments for this, such as antifungal creams, topical steroids, or vaginal estrogen?
“I haven’t tried any prescription treatments yet—only over-the-counter lubricants, which didn’t help. I haven’t used antifungal creams, steroid creams, or vaginal estrogen.”
Do you have any personal history of autoimmune conditions, such as thyroid disease, vitiligo, or alopecia areata?
Patient: I don’t have any diagnosed autoimmune conditions like thyroid disease, vitiligo, or alopecia areata. I’ve just had diet-controlled type 2 diabetes and hypertension.
Do you experience significant vaginal dryness, or have you noticed any unusual vaginal discharge or odor?

“I do feel significant vaginal dryness, and intercourse is very uncomfortable because of that. I haven’t noticed any unusual vaginal discharge or an unusual odor—mainly it’s the severe vulvar itching and irritation.”
[DDX] Lichen sclerosus, Genitourinary syndrome of menopause, Lichen simplex chronicus, Vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia, Contact dermatitis
